identity.title: Grain Size Constraints on HL Tau with Polarization Signature

paper_type_evidence.quote: We construct an axisymmetric dust disk model with several gaps with a smooth temperature distribution which reasonably reproduces the sub-mm continuum image at $\lambda = 1.3 {\rm~mm}$ (cite: Partnership15).

evidence.quote: HL Tau is a protostar 140 pc away from the sun (cite: Rebull04).
HL Tau is a protostar 140 pc away from the sun (cite: Rebull04).

question.value: Can self-scattering of thermal dust emission explain the millimeter-wave polarization of the HL Tau disk, and what maximum grain size does it imply?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we report a modeling of the millimeter-wave polarization of the HL Tau disk with the self-polarization.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV.

bands.value: Band 6 (1.3 mm) continuum, used to calibrate the disk model

evidence.quote: to reproduce the observation along the major axis of the disk observed with the continuum observed with the ALMA Band 6.

provided.value: Polarization degree 0.89% at 1.3 mm, polarization vectors

evidence.quote: The net polarization degree is $0.89 \%$ in average with CARMA, and $0.86 \pm 0.4 \%$ with SMA.
The net polarization degree is $0.89 \%$ in average with CARMA, and $0.86 \pm 0.4 \%$ with SMA.

what.value: ALMA Band 6 1.3 mm continuum image/profile of HL Tau (long baseline campaign)

evidence.quote: reasonably reproduces the sub-mm continuum image at $\lambda = 1.3 {\rm~mm}$ (cite: Partnership15).

what.value: CARMA and SMA polarization measurements of HL Tau

evidence.quote: we successfully reproduced the polarization vectors and polarization degree of HL Tau observed with CARMA and SMA(cite: Stephens14).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: RADMC-3D radiative transfer of an axisymmetric gapped disk model with spherical Mie grains, amax varied

evidence.quote: We perform the radiative transfer simulations with a public code RADMC-3D to obtain the dust continuum, the polarized intensity, and the polarization degree.

what.value: Polarization formula P = C P90 omega and ±50% model uncertainty

evidence.quote: The theoretical model is calculated as the product of polarization degree at $90^\circ$ scattering $P_{90}$ and the albedo $\omega$ (cite: Kataoka15).
The composition is assumed to be the mixture of silicate, organics, and water ice (cite: Kataoka14; Pollack94).

method.value: Power-law temperature and optical depth with 7 Gaussian gaps tuned to the Band 6 major-axis brightness temperature

evidence.quote: Then, we add the additional gaps on the density profile to reproduce the observation along the major axis of the disk observed with the continuum observed with the ALMA Band 6.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute dust opacity and surface density

method.value: Mie theory with Maxwell-Garnett mixing; Sigma_d = tau/kappa_abs(amax,1.3 mm)

evidence.quote: The opacity is calculated with Mie theory.

findings_qualitative.value: Polarization degree is about two times higher in gaps than in rings

evidence.quote: The polarization degree is two times higher in the gap regions than that in ring regions.

claims.hypothesis: Self-scattering can explain HL Tau mm polarization
claims.experiment: RADMC-3D models of a gapped disk
claims.result: Vector direction and degree reproduced for amax ~150 um
claims.finding: Self-scattering is a viable explanation and constrains amax to 70-270 um

evidence.quote: We find that the direction of the polarization vectors and the polarization degree can be explained with the self-scattering.

claims.hypothesis: Polarization grain size is consistent with that from the opacity index
claims.result: beta implies mm-cm sizes, much larger than 150 um
claims.finding: Inconsistent for compact spheres; porous aggregates may reconcile

evidence.quote: We discuss that porous dust aggregates may solve the inconsistency of the maximum grain size between the two constraints.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: amax = 350 um ruled out since it underestimates SMA 0.89 mm polarization

evidence.quote: Therefore, we can rule out the possibility of $a_{\rm max} = 350{\rm~\mu m}$ to explain the polarization.

limitations_admitted.value: Disk model is not a unique solution

evidence.quote: This model is not a unique solution of the density and temperature of the HL Tau disk.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single disk model; no formal fit or uncertainty on amax
Spherical grain assumption drives upper limit
